author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T170438Z-856615
text:
Review-loop deadlock observed 2026-05-11 17:08-17:43Z (run 20260511T170837Z).

What happened:
- /do-beads delegated to bd-review-loop --epic JMAP-sc1b per spec
- bd-review-loop spawned a /review-rusty opencode child session
- The review-readonly agent inside that child tried to run 'RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps'
- Permission overlay returned action="ask"
- Non-interactive opencode run had no one to answer → deadlock
- Parent bd-review-loop hung waiting on the child
- /do-beads bash timeout (35 min) eventually killed the process tree
- Log line: ~/.local/state/bd-review-loop/JMAP/20260511T170837Z/iter-1-review-rusty.log
  ...permission=bash pattern=RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps action={"permission":"bash","pattern":"*","action":"ask"} asking...

Same failure mode the /do-beads spec already documents for the interactive 'question' tool: a non-interactive child needs human input and there's no one to give it.

Convergence state on this epic when the deadlock occurred:
- 0 P0 findings open
- 0 P1 findings open
- 2 P2 chores (examples/, benches/ directory scaffolding sweeps — mechanical work, not review findings)
- 7 P3 findings open
- 1 P4 opinion open

That meets the epic description's convergence criterion ("only P3+ findings or 'opinion' labels") IF the two P2 entries are reclassified as scaffolding sweeps rather than review findings. They look mechanical to me.

Questions for human:

1. Permission gap: should the review-readonly agent definition (or bd-review-loop's spawned opencode invocation) be granted read-only cargo commands (cargo doc, cargo check, cargo clippy) by default? These are non-destructive and central to any Rust review. Recommendation: extend the agent's bash allowlist to include 'cargo doc *', 'RUSTDOCFLAGS=* cargo doc *', 'cargo check *', 'cargo clippy --workspace -- *'. Without this, every future bd-review-loop run will deadlock the same way.

2. Convergence call: is this epic converged? Recommendation: yes — close JMAP-sc1b, leave the 10 open children to be worked individually. The current /do-beads frontier includes JMAP-sc1b.18 (P2 benches) and JMAP-sc1b.104 (P3 AccountInfo PII Debug) at the top of the queue once the parent epic is no longer ready.

Skipping per /do-beads spec (file question as bead, move on).
